_comment: Every number the policy boundary acts on. A threshold buried in code is a
threshold nobody re-calibrates, so they live here and get diffed in review.
The guards sit ON TOP of the abstention band in models/semantic-config.json.
The band decides whether a head answers at all; a guard decides whether an
answer is strong enough to take an action that costs somebody something.
Refusing a real business and sending a standard site to a sales call are
both such actions, so both are guarded; review and unclear are the
fallbacks and need no guard, because doing them wrongly only costs a human
two minutes.
refuseMinLlmConfidence / customMinLlmConfidence apply only when an injected
tier decided (the semantic tier abstained and the caller supplied an LLM).
A model's self-reported confidence is worth less than a calibrated cosine,
so these sit high.
The numbers are READ OFF the held-out distribution, per language, not
guessed, and the lesson of doing that was that SIMILARITY is the wrong
thing to lean on and MARGIN is the right one. On the 2026-09-14 holdout,
rows wrongly called prohibited sat at similarity ~0.17 - which is also
where correctly-classified French and Romanian prohibited rows sit. A
similarity guard tuned on the English distribution does not separate right
from wrong; it separates English from French. Margin does separate them:
wrong rows had margin p25 0.008 while correct ones had p10 0.058 even in
the weakest language.
So each guard's similarity floor is set AT the head's abstention band -
the band already screens similarity, and duplicating that job only
penalises the weakest language - and the margin floor is what actually
guards the action. Same reasoning on the scope head: custom-work is a
tight cluster (margin p05 0.132 in the weakest language) and the rows
wrongly called custom-work were not (margin p25 0.002).
These are cosines in the MEAN-CENTRED space of models/centroids.json, not
raw e5 cosines. They mean nothing against a differently-built centroid set,
and they must be re-read whenever the band is re-swept.
